---
title: "For instructors"
subtitle: "Stable materials, flexible course routes"
description: "Ways to adopt QMSBR across quantitative methods courses without duplicating the source materials."
---

QMSBR is a source library, not a semester syllabus. Keep chapter identities
stable and let each course select its own sequence, pace, and assessed work.

## Three reusable routes

::: {.route-grid}
::: {.route-card}
### Quantitative inquiry foundation

Use Chapters 01–04 to connect evidence, description, sampling, uncertainty,
tests, effect sizes, categorical association, and group comparisons.
:::
::: {.route-card}
### Computing-forward route

When Chapters 05–06 are released, pair them with Chapter 01 and revisit selected
earlier ideas through code before entering regression. They are roadmap items,
not Release 1 downloads.
:::
::: {.route-card}
### Regression bridge

Use Chapters 01–03 as the conceptual spine. Chapters 07–08 will later extend
that spine to simple and conditional regression claims; Chapters 05–06 will add
R support. These chapters are not yet public.
:::
:::

These are starting patterns, not fixed timetables. A 180-minute class can mix
brief explanation, a worked example, interpretation, and guided practice, while
students use the fuller chapter as pre-class or reference reading.

## Website and Moodle have different jobs

| QMSBR website | Moodle or another course space |
|---|---|
| Canonical current chapters | The term sequence and weekly instructions |
| Stable public links | Course announcements and deadlines |
| One representative note example | Course-selected lecture notes |
| Answer-free chapter exercises | Assessment, feedback, and answer keys |

Link to the current website when students should receive corrections
automatically. For a high-stakes or formally approved syllabus, record the
QMSBR release tag so the exact assigned version can be recovered.

## Adoption checklist

- State which chapter version or release your course uses.
- Link to the Library rather than uploading duplicate chapter files when policy
  permits.
- Put course-specific lecture notes and assessments in the controlled course
  space.
- Retain data provenance and licence notices if a later release provides a supplement.
- Cite the collection and the underlying data or studies where appropriate.
- Report an issue when a public correction would help every course using the
  material.
